title: Make a custom pressable control
summary: Pressable can wrap a custom control. Its style callback receives pressed, so the control can show a clear response.
introduction: Pressable can wrap a custom control. Its style callback receives pressed, so the control can show a clear response. Your task: Change the pressed colour while keeping text readable.
learningObjectives: Change the pressed colour while keeping text readable.
Explain the example for make a custom pressable control

blocks.text: Pressable can wrap a custom control. Its style callback receives pressed, so the control can show a clear response.
Use a current Expo project with React Native. Put examples in App.jsx. Run the project with Expo on a supported device or emulator. Native components do not run in this website's HTML playground.

blocks.code:
import {Pressable,Text,View} from "react-native";
export default function App(){return <View style={{padding:24}}><Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={()=>console.log("Chosen")} style={({pressed})=>({padding:16,backgroundColor:pressed?"#12345a":"#174a8b"})}><Text style={{color:"white"}}>Choose a book</Text></Pressable></View>;}
blocks.title: Make a custom pressable control

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `Pressable` supplies press state and actions for a custom native control. Give the control a role and readable label.
`onPress` is the native action callback. It is different from a web button's `onClick` prop.

blocks.text: The control darkens while pressed and logs Chosen when activated.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Give custom controls a role and readable label. Styling alone does not communicate their purpose.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the pressed colour while keeping text readable.
